title: Image scorers relied less on generated descriptions after reward training
summary: Replacing an image’s generated reasoning with a description of another image reduced the rank correlation with human ratings by 0.548 for base 7B Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct and by 0.084 after score-reward training on KADID-10k. The tested 32B model retained greater sensitivity to the swap. The experiment measures dependence on the generated words for these image-scoring tasks.
ai_technology: Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct; reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards
organization: University of Bristol; Jiangxi University of Finance and Economics; China University of Mining and Technology; City University of Hong Kong

source_review.scope: v1 model setup and §5 intervention table

evidence.tested: The paper compares base and score- or rank-reward models on standard image-quality datasets, using donor-chain substitution and other interventions.
evidence.unknown: The experiment tests observable descriptions and task performance. It does not establish reasoning mechanisms for other tasks or model families.
evidence.ai_role: Qwen2.5-VL-Instruct image scorers were trained with verifiable rewards and evaluated with reasoning descriptions swapped across images.
